title: Slice-first dashboard guidelines + instrumentation checklist
body:
Purpose:
This note describes a "slice-first" approach to composing inference dashboards and the accompanying instrumentation checklist required to make those dashboards reliable, low-cost, and actionable. The idea: design dashboards by latency/behavioral slices (fast, cold-cache, long-tail, degraded-fallback) rather than by layers (serve/runtime/kernel). That maps better to operator workflows and SLOs for tokenized inference.

Audience:
- Observability engineers
- Oncall / SREs for inference services
- Runtime/serving engineers who own metrics instrumentation
- Product managers who need SLO-aligned panels

Executive summary (1 paragraph):
Slice-first dashboards prioritize user-visible outcomes: percentiles, error modes, and cost signals per slice. Each slice has a small set of canonical metrics, a tracing anchor, and a compact drilldown recipe. The payoff: faster incident triage, clearer rollouts (canary vs rollout impact per slice), and targeted instrumentation investment (we only pay for traces/metrics where it yields operational value).

Core concepts and rationale:
- Slice = a coherent operational surface that shares a cause and remediation pattern. Examples: 
  * "fast-path" (requests satisfying prefix cache and short sequence)
  * "cold-start" (first tokens with KV miss and model load)
  * "kv-tail" (long-tail requests that touch many KV pages or cause paging)
  * "fallback-routing" (requests routed to cheaper model/region)
  * "token-regression" (quality drop related to prompt length or truncated context)
- Each slice should be represented by: 3–6 primary metrics, 1 trace anchor (sampled spans keyed by reason), and one cost estimate metric.
- Prefer quantile based SLIs (p50/p90/p99) with cohort tagging (tenant, model-version, route) instead of just averages.

Recommended metric set (per slice):
- request_count: counter (tagged: tenant, route, model_version, slice)
- token_emitted_count: counter (tags as above)
- svc_latency_ms: histogram/summary (buckets tuned for slice - see below)
- kv_cache_hit_rate: gauge or ratio (kv_hits / kv_lookups)
- model_loads_per_1k_requests: counter-derived rate (captures cold starts)
- fallback_rate: counter (times routed to fallback variants)
- cost_per_request_usd_estimated: gauge (derived from token_emitted_count * model_unit_cost + infra amortization)

Metric naming conventions (examples):
- Observability prefix: obs.inference.<logical_component>.<metric>
  e.g., obs.inference.request_count, obs.inference.svc_latency_ms.bucketed
- Use dimension keys consistently: tenant_id, model, model_version, route, slice
- Avoid embedding env or region in base name; use tags instead for reuse

Aggregation and bucketing guidance:
- svc_latency_ms should use these bucket ranges by default: [0-5ms, 5-20ms, 20-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-1s, 1s+]. For heavy tail slices add extended buckets up to 10s.
- Store quantiles at 50/90/95/99 with reservoir sampling to keep storage low.
- For cost signals, emit per-request cost estimates at ingestion time (cheap compute) and aggregate by tenant to avoid expensive per-token postprocessing in dashboards.

Tracing conventions (how traces tie to slices and metrics):
- Root span name: inference.request (attributes: tenant_id, route, model, model_version, slice_hint)
- Annotate spans with token-batched boundaries: span.annotations: {token_start, token_end, kv_cache_hit:true|false, model_variant}
- Sampling policy: trace 1% of all traffic globally, but increase to 10% for requests where svc_latency_ms > p99 baseline OR fallback_rate > threshold OR kv_cache_hit_rate below threshold. This ensures higher fidelity for problem slices without exploding costs.
- Span tagging for tracing drilldowns: include trace_anchor_id = concat(route, model_version, slice) so dashboards can request sample traces for the exact panel.

Dashboard composition rules (compact panels per slice):
- Each slice view should include: traffic trend (request_count), latency quantiles (p50/p90/p99), error rate (4xx/5xx/corpus-quality-failures), kv_cache_hit_rate, fallback_rate, cost_per_request_estimated.
- Drilldown button: "Fetch sample traces" should pass trace_anchor_id and a narrow time window, and fallback to a synthetic probe trace when real traces are not available.
- Keep panels to a 6-panel max per slice to reduce cognitive load and query budget.

Query budget and cost controls:
- Limit dashboard panel refresh to no more than once per 30s on default dashboards; for oncall emergency boards allow 5s refresh but gated by a feature flag.
- Use pre-aggregated rollup tables for heavy queries (per-model-hourly, per-tenant-5m) and prefer them over raw event queries.
- Apply panel sampling heuristics: if a tenant has >N requests, show sampled cohort metrics with a clear footer indicating sampling rate.

Ownership and runbook bindings:
- Each slice has an owning team (e.g., serving-runtime, kv-cache, routing) and an oncall alias. Ensure dashboard metadata contains "owner_team" and "oncall_playbook_link" in the panel description.
- A minimal runbook stub for each slice: what to check (kv_cache_hit_rate, model load counts, recent rollouts), initial remediation steps, key traces to inspect.

Instrumentation checklist (what engineering teams must add):
1) Emit obs.inference.request_count with slice tag populated by either router or the first service that can accurately compute the slice (router preferred).
2) Ensure svc_latency_ms uses consistent buckets and exposes histogram or summary with quantiles.
3) Increment kv cache metrics at the cache layer with tags for cache_shard and tenant.
4) Emit model_load events with reason tag (cold_start, reload, evict) and correlate with request_id.
5) Add trace anchors: when a request is classified into a slice, attach trace_anchor_id to the trace root.
6) Implement dynamic tracing sampling action: a lightweight evaluator that marks spans for higher sampling rates when thresholds are hit.
7) Provide a cost_per_request_usd_estimated gauge at the point of token finalization (not retroactively).
8) Add feature flags to enable debug-level telemetry per-tenant for short windows to reduce steady state cost.

Migration and rollout plan for existing dashboards:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): create slice mapping for top 10 routes by traffic. Add slice tags in router logs and emit request_count.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): deploy svc_latency_ms buckets and kv metrics; build a single "slice index" dashboard showing slice distribution.
- Phase 3 (6 weeks): migrate active oncall dashboards to slice-first panels, add trace sampling escalation, and deprecate redundant layer-based panels.

Pruning and lifecycle guidance:
- Auto-deprecation rule: if a panel is not opened by any user and its query execution cost is > X for 90 days, flag for removal.
- Keep a registry (lightweight CSV) of panels with owner and last-accessed timestamp; tie deprecation notifications to owners.

Example queries (pseudocode):
- Request rate by slice (5m rollup): SELECT slice, sum(request_count) FROM obs_inference_rollup_5m WHERE time >= now()-1h GROUP BY slice
- P99 latency for kv-tail by tenant (1h): SELECT quantile(0.99, svc_latency_ms) FROM obs_inference WHERE slice='kv-tail' AND tenant_id='t-123' AND time >= now()-1h

Open questions / tradeoffs (short):
- How many slice categories are minimally sufficient? (goal: keep to 5–8 operational slices to limit cardinality)
- Where to compute slice assignment: router (early) vs runtime (richer context)? Router simplifies early telemetry but may misclassify based on later cache hits.
- Storage cost for per-request cost gauges vs sampled cost estimates.

Appendix: helpful heuristics for teams implementing this
- If you have to choose one signal to instrument first: svc_latency_ms (histogram) wins.
- Add slice hints as enums not freeform strings to reduce cardinality.
- Use tenant-weighted sampling for traces: prefer more traces for higher-revenue tenants but cap total trace volume.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Prototype a "slice classifier library" that runtime and router can import (Ravi owning).
- Create an ingestion job that precomputes per-tenant cost estimates (Maya to own).
- Draft a short training doc for oncall runbook (Ava to draft).

End of document.
